content.thinking:
I need to write this carefully in one pass since I can't test it, sticking to APIs I'm confident about. I'm designing a hunched swamp troll around 2.6 meters tall in a Blizzard-inspired style—chunky build, oversized hands and shoulders, a smaller tusked head with a mohawk, bone fetishes, and a loincloth, with teal-green mottled skin and a magenta accent on the mohawk.

I'm working through the skeleton: hips as the root joint, a spine chain running hips to chest, then neck, head, and jaw, mirrored arms with shoulder/elbow/wrist/hand joints, and IK-driven legs, being careful to use explicit coordinates and consistent left/right mirroring conventions rather than relying on ambiguous local axes. I'm placing the spine's catmull points and deciding how to name the chain segments so hips remains the proper root joint, likely creating hips as a standalone joint first and then attaching the spine chain to it as a child.

I'm sketching the neck as a short chain parented to the last spine joint, then adding a head joint angled forward and downward to give the troll its hunched posture, and roughly blocking out the overall height so the hips sit around 1.2m, the chest tops out near 2.2m, and the head center lands around 2.45m.

Now I'm building the torso as a lofted tube running along the spine path, defining width and height stations at each point from the pelvis up through the belly, adjusting proportions to make the gut bulge out while keeping the shoulders hunched forward.

Then I'm working out the skin shading, using mottled texture for the body with a lighter countershaded belly patch applied specifically to the front-facing, lower-torso region rather than the underside, since a troll's belly faces forward.

For the arms, I'm positioning shoulder, elbow, and wrist joints with slight outward extension and downward hang, planning to connect them as a polyline chain for the limb structure.

Each hand needs fingers and a thumb as separate short chains branching off the wrist joint tip, with claw spikes capping the ends, and the whole arm parented to the chest joint in the spine.

I'm tapering the arm's radius from shoulder to wrist and adding a fist shape at the hand plus a spiky pauldron/shoulder pad made from a half-sphere with bone spikes for armor. Now moving to the legs: hip joints at the sides, knees bending forward, and ankles below.

Setting up the leg chain with named joints and parent hierarchy, using thicker radii tapering down the limb, with feet that touch the ground and claw-like toes built from small spheres and spikes attached at the ankle.

For the head, I'm placing the skull as a scaled sphere, adding a heavy brow ridge box across the top, and starting on the muzzle with a box and frustum shape for the upper jaw before working on the lower jaw.

Shaping the lower jaw and tusks...

Still shaping ear geometry... Now I'm planning the mohawk as spiky strand cards following a spine of frames from forehead to upper back, oriented upward along the curve.

For actual construction I'll build chunky stiffened spikes as cones alternating red and orange, leaning backward along the path, around 14 of them attached to head/neck bones rather than fine strand cards, maybe adding a small fur tuft card set at the shoulders.

Now I'm thinking through fetishes: a bone necklace of beads/teeth arranged around the chest using an elliptical ring of positions dipping in front, built with a helper function for sphere beads, plus small bone totems hanging from the belt made of bundled bones, feathers, and a tiny skull shape built from a sphere and box jaw.

I'm deciding to skip adding a held weapon or staff to keep the pose simple, and instead focus accessories on necklace, belt fetishes, shoulder pad with skull/tusks, wrist and ankle bone bracelets, and leg charms, plus a painted striped loincloth built from extruded flap outlines front and back.

Now I'm working out the geometry for the loincloth flap position relative to the belly and pelvis curvature, adjusting its y/z coordinates and thickness so it hangs naturally off the belt against the body's protruding surface.

For the belt itself, I'm looping around a point on the body surface near the hips, sweeping it into a leather band, then placing brass stud spheres at regular intervals along that path using frame-based positioning.

Staying within the 64 flat-color limit, I'm adding scattered warts across the body as tiny embedded spheres, and considering whether to include spine spikes or a mohawk ridge, though I'll likely skip decal-based scars and just keep a simple chest tattoo decal for war paint.

Now I'm working out the hands: chunky box-shaped palms hanging below the wrist joint, with three-fingered chains curling slightly forward from each palm.

3 fingers + thumb = 4 chains per hand, 2 joints each, times 2 hands gives 16 joints total, which checks out. I'm positioning the arms with shoulder, elbow, and wrist points per side, making sure the hands hang above floor level near knee height, giving a natural arm length of about 1.2 units plus the hand, which fits well against the chest width.

Now I'm defining shoulder, elbow, and wrist joints as a chain parented to the spine, using side-based x positioning for left versus right. I'm setting taper radii for the arm segments so forearms read a bit thicker, and working out how to grab the chain's tip joint cleanly for attaching the hand geometry, planning to mirror the same approach for the legs, and settling on a mossy green-grey skin tone fitting for a swamp troll.

Writing color palette...

Still writing paint helpers...

Still building skin paint and head geometry...

Still placing facial features...

Positioning the ring using the tangent along the bezier curve at a point partway up, scaling the torus radius to match the tusk's taper there. I'm also planning small upper fangs as additional spikes, and considering mohawk color and optional hair cards for the head.

Now I'm laying out the crest's spine as a series of catmull-rom points running from the forehead down toward mid-back, tilting the direction vector backward and varying the spike length as it goes. I'm working out the curve coordinates so the crest tapers down and ends properly near the shoulders, checking how the vertical tube extents relate to the chest station height.

Still writing crest coordinates...

Actually I'll skip the base ridge and instead place flame-shaped tuft cards at each spike point, using an SVG fringe shape colored in red-orange gradients, oriented along the spike frames with a slight lean for flow.

Now I'm sketching a helper function to build a skull fetish: a cranium sphere, a jawbone box offset below and forward, and small eye-socket spheres positioned symmetrically on the face, all assembled relative to a given anchor point and bone.

Then I'm figuring out the necklace geometry—placing bead points in a circular arc around the neck/chest area, adjusting the radius and vertical drape so the beads follow the torso's shoulder width and chest depth naturally.

I'm sweeping the drape path into a leather cord, then placing alternating bone beads and hanging tusk-teeth spikes along it using tangent-facing positions, with a central skull pendant anchored at the front.

Now I'm positioning the skull pendant relative to the drape's starting point, then setting up a belt loop around the hips using a weighted skin point near the spine joint, with additional fetish pieces hanging from angled positions along the belt path.

Shaping the loincloth's jagged front flap with a leather texture, positioning it at the belt's front point with a notched zigzag outline for a tribal look.

I'm checking the back flap placement mirrors the front, computing where the belt sits relative to the body's z-depth at the hip station so the flap hangs flush without floating or clipping into the surface below.

Now I'm adding small details—a brass earring hoop on one ear, and bone bracelet rings as torus shapes wrapped around the forearm near the wrist, positioned using the arm's path tangent and frame orientation so they sit naturally around the limb.

Adding more positioning details...

Binding the deltoid sphere to the arm's shoulder joint so it moves naturally with the arm, with the pad riding over it on the chest. For the back I'm adding a hunched hump using scaled spheres near the upper spine plus a trapezius bump behind the head, then considering a ridge of small spike cones along the dorsal spine for texture.

I'm using the torso sweep's "along" function to place six spikes right along the back's dorsal normal, alternating moss and bone colors for the ridge. Then I'm planning skin warts scattered across the torso and a tribal war-paint decal on the chest using a small SVG texture.

Now I'm figuring out the decal placement and projection direction against the torso surface, then moving on to leg construction with tapering thigh sweeps and feet built from a box plus toe spheres with clawed spikes projecting forward.

I'm positioning the toe spikes so their bases sit just above the floor, verifying the foot box bottom aligns exactly to y=0 for solid ground contact, and placing the ankle joint capping the leg tube. Then I'm setting up the joint hierarchy—hip, knee, ankle—parented under the hips root for the leg chain.

Now I'm working out the limb function's root points and bend directions: using the point array as a polyline for the chain, wrapping the knee bend direction as a single-item list, and checking that the root/target positions with given segment lengths produce a forward knee bend matching the actual distance between joints.

For the torso, I'm planning the hip and belly loft stations with increasing width and depth going up (a big gut shape), then setting up the spine joint chain to start at the same point as the hips joint so the bone and loft path align, using a catmull spline through the spine control points.

Moving to the neck and head, I'm setting a short two-span neck joint chain that tapers with a sweep, then attaching a head skull sphere forward and above the neck's end point, overlapping slightly for a solid connection. I'm scaling the head smaller relative to the shoulders for a troll-like proportion, and calculating the total height with the mohawk included to land around 3.1-3.15 units tall.

I'm then checking the jaw, muzzle, and teeth placement so the mouth closes naturally without gaps, nudging the muzzle frustum slightly upward so it overlaps properly with the lower jaw and tusks sit outside correctly.

Working out tusk curve positions...

Setting up the eye sockets with a dark sphere recess, a small glowing sphere for the eye itself, and a tiny dark pupil box, positioned just under the brow and checking placement so it reads clearly on the head.

Adding angled brow capsules for an angry slant, then placing ears at the sides and considering whether to skip cheeks, chin beard, and under-eye details, maybe adding small warts to the head.

For decoration, I'm skipping head tattoos but adding a skull fetish on the shoulder pad, plus a pendant skull and belt bundles, with a feather card texture hanging from the bundles and shoulder using angled frame cards for the hanging effect.

Now I'm working out knee spike placement, positioning the spike base slightly forward of the knee joint using offset coordinates derived from the leg chain's joint position.

I'm skipping mesh merging given the part count stays well under budget, and deciding to represent moss patches as painted skin color rather than separate geometry. For mud stains, I'm setting up a paint function that blends the base skin color toward a mud tone based on height, using a smoothstep so the mud intensifies near the feet and fades higher up the leg.

Now I'm defining painted material helpers for leather and bone accessories, layering mottled base textures with lighter and darker paint tones for added surface variation.

I'm checking that the smoothstep edge values work correctly for a decreasing range, then sketching the hand geometry—building a palm box and positioning it relative to the wrist joint bone.

Now I'm laying out finger and thumb positions: each finger as a chain of base, mid, and tip points curving forward and down toward the floor, with the thumb following a similar bent path offset to the side.

Still defining finger chains and claws...

Adding an ankle band torus with leather/brass material, checking it overlaps the foot box properly, then starting the torso's painted shader with a belly highlight region.

Blending base skin tone with belly color based on normal and vertical position, mixing by a smoothstep weight. After that I'll add scattered warts on the upper torso, filtered to avoid the lower body area.

Still writing spike placement logic...

I'm confirming the torso sweep covers the full length including the neck hump, then moving on to finalize smaller details—skipping a tail, adding a loincloth tassel, checking the foot-to-thigh gap, and setting the eye glow intensity with slit-shaped black pupils.

Positioning the nose and nostrils...

I'm sketching SVG textures for feather and tuft patterns, then designing a claw-slash decal with diagonal strokes and a circle outline for detailing. I'll skip tribal forearm marks for now and set up the final export with metadata and skeleton joint type imports.

Checking that all my imports are actually used, I'm tying noise and mottle functions into a mossy skin blend variant, layering noise thresholds over the base mottled texture to create patchy coloring.

I need to watch for unused-parameter typecheck errors, underscoring params not used in each paint callback, and making sure functions like frame, offset, and the skin paints are defined in the right order before being referenced in the ring and spike callbacks.

Working out forearm ring placement: the chain point at t=0.78 gives a radius around .17, so I'm sizing the torus (radius .19, tube .035) and outward spikes to sit just outside the forearm surface without sinking in.

For the hanging bundle helper, I'm defining a function that builds a cord from the anchor point downward with a leather rod, then adds a few bone capsules fanning outward with slight offsets per index, optionally a small skull for certain bundles, and feather cards framed off the same anchor — all generated once per bundle call.

Now I'm figuring out the belt: it loops around the torso surface at a given height with a slight lift, following the path's weights so the sweep bends naturally with the body, and I'm placing a skull plate as a buckle at the front of that belt loop.

For the studs, I realize the first loop radius makes them sit hidden inside the band, so I need a second loop with a larger lift radius so the studs poke out visibly, spaced evenly around using the "along" helper and weighted to the hip bones.

Now I'm sketching out fetishSkull as a helper that builds a small cranium sphere, a tiny maxilla and mandible box, dark eye sockets, and a nose bump, all positioned and bone-weighted together. Setting up the imports for the builder, frame, math, path, IK, paint utilities, skeleton types, texture, and glow kit needed for this piece.

Checking that skeleton exports Chain and Joint types correctly, then defining the color palette constants before starting the build function. I'm laying out the skeleton hierarchy: hips as the root joint, a three-segment spine chain via catmull spline, a chest reference point, a two-segment neck chain, then head and jaw joints with specific positions and aim targets, followed by the start of a lofted torso mesh bound to the hip and spine bones.

Now I'm sweeping the neck bones with skin coloring, adding a spherical hump shape near the chest for the troll's hunched back, and planning the arm and leg loops. For legs, I'm computing limb points for hip-knee-ankle placement, building a chain with matching joint names per side, sweeping it with tapering radii for a leg shape, then starting to construct a foot box geometry attached at the ankle.

Adding toe spheres and claw spikes...

Adding spike ring around the shoulder pad at the ellipsoid's edge, tilted outward, with the pad attached to the chest since arms rotate independently. Also adding a torus trim ring around the pad.

Now I'm shaping the mohawk crest using a Catmull-Rom spline, placing thirteen spikes along it with lengths varying sinusoidally and directions tilting backward toward the crown but angling forward near the forehead.

Still writing spike geometry...

Building a closed catmull-rom loop for the necklace drape, computing a ring of points around the neck with slight vertical sag based on cosine falloff.

I'm checking the loop's edge cases against the torso geometry—points at the front, sides, and back all land close enough to the body surface to snap correctly during the drape computation. Now I'm setting up the drape call with a small lift offset before moving into the cord sweep logic.

Adding spikes and skull pendant to the necklace...

Still defining paint colors...

I'm fixing the negative modulo issue with Math.abs for the stripe pattern, then adding a decal placement for the war emblem on the torso before returning the finished build.

Now I'm writing a fetishSkull helper that builds a skull shape from a sphere and jaw box, with dark eye sockets and a small nose detail, using a dark bone color.

Checking that the builder methods like sweep, spike, and capsule have signatures that fit, then writing the rest of the bundle bones code using these helpers.
